Tree shadow is a literal rgba(0,0,0,0.3); no Signal token (creature shadow is 0.38).
Ground-lettering alphas (9%, 45%, 50%, 30%, needs-you 95%), café checker (3.5%), lit-window alpha (50%), lit fraction (20%) and lit threshold (night > 0.15) are literals with no Signal tokens.
Textures stipple and lines have no --sg-overview-opacity-texture-* token; they fall back to a literal 0.07.
Speech type (mono 400 10.5px, 18px tall) has no Signal type or size token; --sg-type-badge is 500/lh 1 and --sg-size-map-label is 18px but is not referenced.
Popover shadow literal 0 10px 28px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55) differs from --sg-shadow-popover (0 8px 24px -8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)).
Tooltip and toast shadows, durations, layout insets, zoom constants, label gap and callout limit are written as literals equal to Signal values instead of var(--sg-*)/getComputedStyle.

Edge markers use --sg-status-*-border (40%); Signal --sg-overview-opacity-edge-marker-border is 45%. Failed hover uses --sg-status-err-bg; Signal has no overview err wash to match --sg-overview-wait-wash-hover.
Label clearance is 6px in the build; Signal --sg-overview-layout-label-gap is 7px.
Minimap viewport is Dim at full opacity, 1.5px; Signal --sg-overview-opacity-viewport describes 70%.
Rail tab bar is 34px; Signal --sg-size-tab-bar is 32px.

Signal extension tokens no longer used by v4: terrain-island-top, terrain-commons, prop-bench-*, plate-session-inset/-pitch, district-*, hud-readout, slab-done-mark, opacity-commons-edge (read but unused), opacity-slab-*, opacity-callout-border, opacity-leader-line; --sg-overlay-label is read at boot but unused; GLYPH.sun is defined but unused.
Off-scale values: task checkbox radius 4px and 1.5px border; tracker input 30px; scrollbar thumb radius 4px.
Canvas fallback hexes in core.js/creatures.js and the task check stroke duplicate Signal values.

narrative.overview:
Overview is a measured plane that a small society lives on. The fleet of agent sessions sits on a 2:1 isometric lattice with a graticule at the stage edges. Each machine is a neighbourhood generated from its id: a tinted ground with its own texture, a skyline of closed buildings along the back, project offices as low open-front rooms, a café, a canteen or a park, streets between the lots, and bridges to its neighbours that carry the SSH latency. Each session is a small grey pixel creature, seeded from its session id, that works at its office desk while it is needed and otherwise lives in the neighbourhood: it gets coffee, eats lunch at the real lunch hour, naps in the park, greets and comforts friends, and talks about the real sessions. Names are painted on the ground like a country on a map. Only what needs the owner floats.

Every colour, face, radius and duration comes from Signal (@barrymind/signal 0.1.2). Core tokens (`--sg-surface-*`, `--sg-text-*`, `--sg-border-*`, `--sg-accent-*`, `--sg-status-*`, `--sg-font-*`) dress the chrome. The Overview extension (`--sg-overview-*`) dresses the plane: neighbourhood tints (`--sg-overview-hood-*`), terrain, lattice, creature coats and slabs. The CSS aliases them to short local names (`--bg`, `--panel`, `--wait` and so on), and the canvas reads them through `getComputedStyle` at boot. Overview owns layout, geometry and behaviour, not values. The chrome has instrument-panel density: 13px body, 11px metadata, 24 to 40px bars and 12px insets.

The world is muted and the signals are loud. Each neighbourhood carries one low-chroma tint on its ground, walls and roofs. Day and night follow the owner's clock and darken only the world. Status hues and the periwinkle accent are never shaded and never decorative, so a raised hand reads the same at noon and at midnight.
keyCharacteristics: Signal 0.1.2 is the token source; Overview references `--sg-*` variables and owns none of the values
2:1 isometric projection, 16 x 8 px per grid unit at 1x, integer device-pixel zoom steps
Machines as generated neighbourhoods (tint, texture, skyline, offices, café, canteen or park, streets, bridges)
Names painted on the ground in perspective; only callouts and speech float
Seeded pixel creatures with a monochrome genome, expressions, emotes and a social life that desk states override
Day and night from the real clock, shading terrain and buildings only
Mono for data, controls and the map; sans for human sentences
Hairlines (1px) and small radii (3 to 6px); flat chrome, soft shadows only on floating overlays

rules.name: The Muted World, Loud Status Rule
rules.body: Each neighbourhood gets one low-chroma tint, and it lands only on terrain, walls and roofs. Saturated hue is spent on the four statuses and the accent and nowhere else: never on creatures, furniture, emotes, speech or signage. If a new element is not a status and not the owner's own selection or action, it is graphite or its neighbourhood's tint.

rules.name: The Loudest Yellow Rule
rules.body: Needs-you yellow outranks everything. Only a waiting session gets the diamond, the ground ring, the hop, a yellow edge marker, a yellow callout and a place in the painted needs-you count. Failed sessions get the coral callout, the coral edge marker and the melt; no other state may borrow these devices.

rules.name: The Night Spares Status Rule
rules.body: Night shades the world (terrain, slabs, floors, walls, buildings, furniture, trees, bridges) toward `--sg-overview-hood-shared-night`. Creatures, slabs, status colours, the accent, ground lettering and every floating label are never shaded.

rules.name: The Signal Source Rule
rules.body: Every colour comes from a `--sg-*` variable. If a needed value is missing, add it to Signal's tokens and rebuild the package; do not write a literal into Overview.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Machines Rule
rules.body: If the text is a name, path, coordinate, number, command or control, it is JetBrains Mono. Instrument Sans is for sentences a person reads.

rules.name: The Painted Names Rule
rules.body: Places are named on the ground, in perspective, never on floating labels. Machine names are territory-sized and faint; project and amenity names sit on their floors. Only callouts (why a hand is raised or a session failed) and speech float above the plane.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates (ages, counts, zoom, coordinates, latency, the clock) uses tabular figures. Graticule coordinates are zero-padded to two digits with a true minus sign (−08).

rules.name: The Generated Neighbourhood Rule
rules.body: A neighbourhood's tint, texture, skyline and amenities come from its machine id, so the same machine always looks the same. Rooms stand at integer grid coordinates and are placed automatically; nothing is dragged.

rules.name: The Integer Pixel Rule
rules.body: Creatures, terrain, rooms and the lattice share one integer device-pixel scale. Never smooth a sprite or offer a zoom between levels.

rules.name: The Label Priority Rule
rules.body: Only two things float, placed in order: callouts first, speech last. Each tries its candidate spots in order and takes the first one that is on screen (2px inset) and clear by 6px of the HUD, the edge markers, the graticule bands (top 26px, left 52px), other creatures and labels already placed. Callouts try above, then right with a leader line, then left, and are forced on screen if their creature is. Speech that finds no spot falls back to a glyph bubble and never covers a callout.

rules.name: The Flat Chrome Rule
rules.body: Bars, rail, cards, chips, rows and buttons are flat. A shadow appears only on something floating above the stage, and state is shown with rings, borders and washes, never lift.

dos: Do reference every colour, face, radius and size through a `--sg-*` variable, and add missing values to Signal rather than to Overview.
Do give each neighbourhood exactly one tint from `--sg-overview-hood-*` and apply it only to its ground, walls and roofs.
Do paint place names on the ground: the machine name territory-sized at 9% Ink, projects and amenities on their floors.
Do keep zoom on the integer levels (k / devicePixelRatio, k in 1 to 8) and draw sprites with image smoothing off.
Do reserve yellow for sessions that need the owner, and give every waiting session all of its signals: diamond, ring, callout, edge marker when off screen, card in the rail and the painted count.
Do keep callouts to 20 characters or fewer and say why the hand is raised ("run pnpm db:migrate?").
Do place speech at the lowest label priority, as words from 1.5x and a glyph below.
Do shade only the world toward night; leave creatures, slabs, status, accent and labels at full value.
Do let desk states override the simulation: a session that needs the owner, runs or fails goes back to its desk.
Do open on the urgent agents when the whole world will not fit at a legible zoom.
Do give every creature on the map a matching row or card in the rail.
donts: Don't write a literal colour or font into Overview when a Signal token exists.
Don't use a status hue or the accent for decoration (emote glyphs, furniture lights, signage); the world is graphite and muted tints.
Don't bring back floating machine or project labels; only callouts and speech float.
Don't let textures, lettering or tints compete with status; textures stay at or below 12% Ink and territory names at 9%.
Don't smooth, rotate or fractionally scale creature sprites.
Don't add drop shadows or lift to bars, cards, chips, rows or buttons; only floating overlays above the stage get a shadow.
Don't set readable text in Faint; it is for the "$" prompt and ambient marks only.
Don't let the tracker act on an agent; it only tracks.
